steps.title: The pattern
say: Point-to-point messaging sends each message to one destination, usually a queue, and each message is taken by exactly one receiver. The queue holds the message until the receiver is ready. On Solace, the recommended form is a topic mapped to a queue: the sender publishes to a topic, one queue subscribes to it, and the sender never names the queue.
This tour takes about ten minutes. Each step tells you what to do, waits while you do it, and then explains what you see. Press Continue when you are ready.

steps.title: The print job
say: This is the shop's label printing. The Order Service needs a shipping label printed for every order, by the Label Printer. That is work for one known service, not news for whoever is interested.
So the Order Service publishes each print job to one topic. One queue on the broker subscribes to that topic, and the Label Printer is that queue's one reader. No other app sees the jobs.

steps.title: Run it
steps.do: Press Play, at the top of the page under Run it.

expect.note: Not everything is running yet. Play takes a few seconds.

say: Press Play. It creates the queue on the broker and subscribes it to the topic, starts the Label Printer, and then the Order Service, which publishes a job every half second.
Press Continue when the dots on the diagram are moving.

steps.title: A sender that knows only the topic
steps.do: Click logs on the Order Service node.

expect.note: The Order Service log is not open yet.

say: Click logs on the Order Service node. Each line is one label job. The Order Service published it to the topic shown on the arrow in the diagram, and waited for the broker to accept it.

It never names the queue, and it does not wait for the printer. That is the recommended form at work: the queue can change without touching the sender. A sender can also address a queue directly by its name, but then it is tied to that one queue.

steps.title: The one receiver
steps.do: Click logs on the Label Printer node.

expect.note: The Label Printer log is not open yet.

say: Now click logs on the Label Printer node. It prints one label at a time, and checks that the job numbers follow on.

steps.title: The queue in between
steps.do: Look at the queue box inside the broker.
say: Look at the queue inside the broker. It subscribes to the Order Service's topic, so every job lands on it. The number beside it is how many jobs are waiting. While the printer keeps up, it stays near zero.

The broker keeps each job until the printer has taken it and acknowledged it. If the printer crashed before acknowledging a job, the broker would send that job again, so the printer must tolerate the occasional repeat.

expect.note: The apps are not both running. Press Play first.

steps.title: Take the printer offline
steps.do: Open the card The printer goes offline, and press Break it.

expect.note: The card is not in effect yet. Open it and press Break it.

say: Now break it. Scroll to Break it, open the card called The printer goes offline, and press Break it.
The Label Printer stops. The Order Service keeps sending.

steps.title: The queue holds the jobs, up to a point
steps.do: Watch the waiting count on the queue, and the Order Service log beside the diagram, for about half a minute.
say: At first nothing goes wrong. The Order Service keeps sending, and the jobs wait on the queue. Watch the waiting count climb.

Keep watching for about twenty seconds. The queue has a size limit. When it is reached, the log beside the diagram shows jobs refused, with the words: Spool Over Quota. The broker tells the sender, and does not keep those jobs.

expect.note: The card is not in effect, so there is nothing to see yet.

steps.title: What comes back, and what does not
steps.do: Press Reset, in the bar at the top of the page.

expect.note: The printer is not back yet. Press Reset in the bar at the top.

say: Press Reset, then open the Label Printer's log from its node. It prints every job that waited, in order. Then it reports a gap: a run of job numbers that never arrived.
The jobs in the gap are the ones the broker refused. They were never stored, so they can never be printed. A queue protects a receiver that is away, but only up to its limit.

steps.title: Get the topic wrong
steps.do: Open the card The sender gets the topic wrong, and press Break it.

expect.note: The card is not in effect yet. Open it and press Break it.

say: The topic is the only thing that ties this sender to its receiver. Open the card called The sender gets the topic wrong, and press Break it.
The Order Service restarts with its topic misspelt, and publishes every job there.

steps.title: A topic no queue subscribes to
steps.do: Read the Order Service log beside the diagram.
say: Every job is refused at once, with the words: No Subscription Match. No queue subscribes to that topic, so nothing would take the job. The printer prints what was already waiting, and then nothing more.
Such a message is normally dropped without a word. This broker is set to refuse it back to the sender, so you can see every job bounce.

expect.note: The card is not in effect, so there is nothing to see yet.

steps.title: Put the topic right
steps.do: Press Reset, in the bar at the top of the page.

expect.note: The card is still in effect. Press Reset in the bar at the top.

say: Press Reset. The Order Service restarts with the right topic, and jobs flow again.

steps.title: When to use it
say: That is point-to-point. Use it when a piece of work belongs to one known service: print a label, send an invoice.
The cost is a queue for each kind of consumer. And one receiver is kept by how the broker is set up, not by the sender: a second queue subscribed to the same topic would get a copy of every job.
Press Cleanup when you are done, or pick another pattern from the sidebar.
